# Fixture format

Unit tests never touch the network (`tests/conftest.py` blocks sockets and sets `OFFLINE=1`).
Each source test records anonymised responses here and replays them through a fake
`HttpClient`.

## Layout

```
tests/fixtures/
  <source>/                 # arxiv, crossref, openalex, ... (one folder per Source.name)
    <case>.json             # metadata of one recorded exchange (see below)
    <case>.body.<ext>       # raw response body (xml, json, html, txt)
  pdfs/                     # synthetic PDFs generated by conftest helpers (never real papers)
  vault/                    # fake Avenox vault with a stub beyin.py for L7b tests
```

## `<case>.json`

```json
{
  "request": {"method": "GET", "url": "https://api.example.org/works", "params": {"filter": "..."}},
  "response": {"status": 200, "headers": {"Content-Type": "application/json"}, "body_file": "<case>.body.json"},
  "expect": {"records": 3, "first_title": "..."}
}
```

* Secrets never appear in fixtures (headers such as `Authorization` are stripped before saving).
* No real person names; DOIs only when they are public demo identifiers (e.g. the Crossref/ORCID
  demo author 0000-0002-1825-0097) or clearly fictional (`10.0000/example.1`).
* Fixture files are UTF-8, NFC-normalised, `ensure_ascii=False`.

## Fake HttpClient

`tests/unit/fakes.py::FixtureHttp` is a `kallimachos.interfaces.HttpClient` implementation that
answers from this folder and raises on an unrecorded URL.
